function: Beamforming design at multi-antenna THz APs by multi-agent DDPG (Prim-CAC) maximizing sum-rate, trained jointly with DRL bitrate selection and PFL viewport prediction (pp. 7-8, 11).
system: Indoor 10x10x4 m room, three ceiling APs with Nt=6 ULA, six users' HMDs with Nr=2, LoS THz channel at 1.05 THz, no RIS (pp. 4, 12).
method: Multi-agent DDPG with LSTM actor-critic: Mac-IAICC (bitrate, CTDE) and Prim-CAC (beamforming, centralized) in a hierarchical DRL framework; viewport GRU trained by personalized federated learning (pp. 9-12).
data_channel: Custom LoS THz channel (spreading and molecular absorption, ULA steering vectors); public 360-degree video dataset [14] (104 videos, 27 viewers' gaze) supplies head-movement data (pp. 4, 12).
test_conditions: Viewport model: 80 training, 24 test videos per user; DRL: 5000 episodes; sweeps of buffer threshold, users up to 12, AP subsets; retraining per setting not stated (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE beamforming [25],[33], combined-FoV priority-based bitrate adaptation [8]; learned: FedAvg-trained viewport prediction [15]; no learned beamforming baseline (p. 13).
metrics: Average QoE, viewport tile quality, intra/inter-chunk quality switch, rebuffering delay, average sum-rate, tile overlap percentage (pp. 13-15).
complexity: Big-O order of online actor-network inference for beamforming: O(d_in d_h + d_h^2 + d_h d_fc + d_fc d_out), with d_h=1024, d_fc=d_out=512 (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 4: "we consider only the LoS path to obtain the THz channel gain", from spreading and molecular absorption losses; custom ULA model, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "we consider 80 and 24 videos in the training dataset" and test dataset, a held-out part of the same data; pp. 13-14 (Figs. 10-12) vary buffer threshold, users, APs, but never state that trained policies are tested on a new setting.
q3_support: p. 15: "we replace the DDPG-based beamforming design algorithm with a WMMSE-based beamforming algorithm"; the only learned benchmark, p. 13: "we use FedAvg to train the head movement prediction model as proposed in [15]", is for viewport prediction, not beamforming.
q4_support: p. 12: "the computational complexity of the online design of beamforming vectors using the pre-trained actor network" is O(dJin dJh + (dJh)^2 + dJh dJfc + dJfc dJout).
q5_support: p. 12: "We conduct our experiments using a public 360° video dataset [14]", a dataset of the viewport-prediction task, not of channels; the THz channel is simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v2 (arXiv:2401.13114, 7 Dec 2024) with the header 'Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications'; no DOI printed, topic and venue consistent. Included: the learned beamforming (Prim-CAC) is a physical-layer decision learned jointly with bitrate selection, which passes above_phy; PFL here is digital, so not area 7; area 3. q3 is 0 because the learned benchmark (FedAvg [15]) is for viewport prediction and is a variant of the proposed PFL training; if the reviewer judges 'same class' for the whole streaming approach it could change. q5 is borderline: the dataset is public eye-gaze data, not channel data.
